|Errors
|`entropy_unavailable`, `errc::not_supported`
|none: it returns `bool`
|none
|its values are the errors
|`invalid_encoding`, `invalid_input_size`
|`memory_functions_refused`, `memory_functions_not_installed`
|`verify`: `invalid_signature`, and `invalid_public_key` for 32 x-only bytes that are no point; `sign`: `invalid_state`, `entropy_unavailable` (Schnorr's drawn randomness), `backend_failure`; a scheme and an input that do not go together stop the build
|`keypair`: none, a concept checked at compile time; `agree`: what the key pair's `agree` returns, and a peer it does not take stops the build
|the member's: `from_secret<K>(bytes)` returns what `K::from_secret(bytes)` returns, `from_bytes<T>(bytes)` what `T::from_bytes(bytes)` returns, `from_key<C>(key)` what `C::from_key(key)` returns, `generate<K>()` what `K::generate()` returns

|Choose it when
|you need a random number an attacker must not predict; never `std::mt19937` or `rand` (link:https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/338.html[CWE-338, a weak generator used for security])
|you compare anything secret; never `==` or `memcmp` on a MAC
|a secret sits in a `std::string`, a `std::vector` or an array of the program's and must not outlive its use; never `memset`, which the optimiser may drop
|you branch on a failure: forged data, a wrong size, no entropy
|a key goes to or comes from a file, a form or a tool as `-----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----` text; with the `encode_spki` and `encode_pkcs8` of `curves::ed25519`, `curves::x25519`, `curves::secp256k1` or `curves::p256`
|a native program on OpenSSL must allocate only from its own arena; on WebAssembly, BearSSL allocates nothing
|a key pair signs with `key_pair.sign(scheme, input)` or `sign(key_pair, scheme, input)`, and a signature is checked with `public_key.verify(scheme, signature, input)` or `verify(scheme, signature, input, public_key)`; a digest computed elsewhere, such as a Bitcoin sighash, an Ethereum EIP-191 digest or the SHA-512 Ed25519ph signs, goes in marked as `prehashed`, never as a bare span; the two recoverable schemes have no `verify`: their signature gives its key to `curves::secp256k1::recover`
|a template takes any curve's key pair: `from_secret`, `generate`, a typed `public_key()` that `verify` takes, `secret()`, and `sign(scheme, input)`; `agree(key_pair, peer)` is the free form of `key_pair.agree(peer)`
|generic code makes any key pair, public key or AEAD by its type, each factory named by its input, or draws a key pair, `generate<K>()`; the free forms of the static members `from_secret`, `from_bytes`, `from_key` and `generate`
